newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-RTZ-CRA to meet on zinc mine.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-RTZ-CRA to meet on zinc mine.

text.p: RTZ Corp Plc-CRA Ltd said on Wednesday it has been invited by one the Aboriginal groups involved in negotiations over development of the Century zinc project in northwest Queensland to meet on Friday.
"We've received an invitation from the Waanyi people and we have accepted", a spokesman for RTZ-CRA unit Century Zinc Ltd told Reuters.

The Waanyi people in the past have been one of several Aboriginal groups that have expressed an interest in reaching an agreement with the Anglo-Australian resources company to allow for the mine's development.
A source close to the talks said it was a positive development in the long-running effort to see the A$1 billion project get off the ground.
Negotiations collapsed on February 13 after only four of 12 Aboriginal groups endorsed a A$60 million jobs and compensation package offerd by Century Zinc in exchange for a guarantee of land title.
As a result, the matter is expected to go before a Federal Native Title tribunal empowered to hand down a binding decision within six months.
Under Australia's native title legislation, indigenous people can claim ownership of leasehold properties to which they can prove historical links.
An agreement among all 12 groups could see the arbitration period cancelled and the mine's development proceed.
The meeting is expected to take place in Doomadgee, Queensland, near the mine site.
RTZ-CRA has said a deal to sell the Century project to Pasminco Ltd could collapse if the talks failed.

Pasminco, the world's biggest zinc producer, had earlier planned to buy half of the mine's annual output of 780,000 tonnes of low iron-bearing concentrates to feed its Budel zinc smelter in the Netherlands.
It later agreed to purchase the project for A$345 million, pending claim-free title to the site and access to land covering a slurry pipeline leading to a port on the Gulf of Carpentaria coast.
Century's development is crucial to the continued operation of the Budel smelter, whose current operating licence requires it to cease generating hazardous jarosite zinc residue.
If development work was to start on the mine in the next few months, production could commence in the latter part of the year 2000, Century Zinc has said.
Pasminco said the collapse of talks were potentially damaging, but could still meet its deadline if things progressed within the next six months.
